prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 2D merge · Clinic schedule (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Time" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Monday" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Tuesday" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Cardiology clinic (Dr. I" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Dermatology" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Staff training — closed " spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Time" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 44px
  col 2: header "Monday › Room A" · longest unbreakable word 74px · one-line width 378px
  col 3: header "Monday › Room B" · longest unbreakable word 87px · one-line width 87px
  col 4: header "Tuesday › Room A" · longest unbreakable word 98px · one-line width 98px
  col 5: header "Tuesday › Room B" · longest unbreakable word 89px · one-line width 367px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A two-day clinic schedule: time rows crossed with Monday/Tuesday and Room A/B columns, showing which clinic is running, when walk-ins are accepted, and when the clinic is closed.","reading":"Readers scan down the Time column for a slot, then across the day/room columns to compare availability. Merged day headers and multi-row clinic cells mean the table is read in blocks rather than cell by cell; the multi-row cells can absorb some prose wrapping before the schedule becomes too tall.","groups":["col 1 (Time) is the row axis and should stay narrow and stable","cols 2–3 form the Monday block, with Room A and Room B as parallel slots under one merged Monday header","cols 4–5 form the Tuesday block, with Room A and Room B as parallel slots under one merged Tuesday header","cols 2 and 5 carry the long clinic prose; cols 3 and 4 are short/empty slots but still carry day/room headers"],"keep_intact":["time labels 09:00, 10:00, 11:00","day names Monday/Tuesday and room labels Room A/Room B where possible","clinic names and identifiers such as Cardiology, Dermatology, Dr. Ito","merged-cell relationships: Monday/Tuesday group their two rooms, and multi-row clinic cells stay associated with their time span"],"may_wrap":["long clinic descriptions such as 'Cardiology clinic (Dr. Ito), walk-ins accepted until 10:30'","the 'Staff training — closed to patients' note","day/room headers may wrap after '›' or between words; avoid splitting words when possible"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[65,110,37,37,110],"idea":"No-scroll content-first fit: keep Time intact and give the two long clinic columns equal width, accepting severe header splits in the two narrow room-only columns."},{"name":"B","widths":[65,140,120,120,140],"idea":"Symmetric day-block scroll layout: each day gets equal width, the long outer room columns get more space, and the inner columns are wide enough to preserve all day/room header words."},{"name":"C","widths":[65,399,108,119,388],"idea":"Full one-line scroll layout: every cell stays on one line, preserving exact wording and the merged-block shape at the cost of a very wide table."}]}
